NLT.8: If she is unwilling to come back with you, then you are free from this oath of mine. But under no circumstances are you to take my son there.”

AMP.4: but you will [instead] go to my [former] country (Mesopotamia) and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son Isaac [the heir of the covenant promise]."
AMP.5: The servant said to him, "Suppose the woman will not be willing to follow me back to this country; should I take your son back to the country from which you came?"

AMP.9: So the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and swore to him concerning this matter.
AMP.10: Then the servant took ten of his master's camels, and set out, taking some of his master's good things with him; so he got up and journeyed to Mesopotamia [between the Tigris and the Euphrates Rivers], to the city of Nahor [the home of Abraham's brother].
AMP.11: He made the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water at the time of the evening when women go out to draw water.
AMP.12: And he said, "O LORD, God of my master Abraham, please grant me success today, and show lovingkindness (faithfulness) to my master Abraham.
AMP.13: Behold, I stand here at the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water;
AMP.14: now let it be that the girl to whom I say, 'Please, let down your jar so that I may [have a] drink,' and she replies, 'Drink, and I will also give your camels water to drink'—may she be the one whom You have selected [as a wife] for Your servant Isaac; and by this I will know that You have shown lovingkindness (faithfulness) to my master."
AMP.15: Before Eliezer had finished speaking (praying), Rebekah came out with her [water] jar on her shoulder. Rebekah was the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, who was the wife of Abraham's brother Nahor.
AMP.16: The girl was very beautiful, a virgin and unmarried; and she went down to the spring and filled her jar and came up.
AMP.17: Then the servant ran to meet her, and said, "Please let me drink a little water from your jar."
AMP.18: And she said, "Drink, my lord"; and she quickly lowered her jar to her hand, and gave him a drink.
AMP.19: When she had given Eliezer a drink, she said, "I will also draw water for your camels until they have finished drinking."
AMP.20: So she quickly emptied her jar into the trough, and ran again to the well and drew water for all his camels.
AMP.21: Meanwhile, the man stood gazing at Rebekah in [reverent] silence, [waiting] to know if the LORD had made his trip successful or not.
AMP.22: When the camels had finished drinking, Eliezer took a gold ring weighing a half-shekel and two bracelets for her hands weighing ten shekels in gold,
AMP.23: and said, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me, is there room in your father's house for us to lodge?"
AMP.24: And she said to him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel, Milcah's son, whom she bore to [her husband] Nahor."
AMP.25: Again she said to him, "We have plenty of both straw and feed, and also room to lodge."
AMP.26: The man bowed his head and worshiped the LORD.
AMP.27: He said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not denied His lovingkindness and His truth to my master. As for me, the LORD led me to the house of my master's brothers."
